paragraph: Closter is a single-family town. Forty-nine detached homes closed over six months at a median of $1,338,000, with a sale-to-list ratio of 1.00, 45 percent of homes going above asking, and a median of 17 days on market. That combination is competitive but not frenzied. Well-priced homes move quickly, and sellers are generally getting their number without a bidding war on every listing. The spread runs from $670,000 to $4,288,000, so the median is the better guide than the range. Volume built the way it usually does here, with three to five closings a month through early spring and then 13, 11, and 14 in May, June, and July. Those spring months are too thin to read on their own, but June and July both held medians above $1.3 million on the heaviest volume of the period, which points to a mix shift toward larger homes rather than softening. If Closter follows the usual seasonal arc, expect closings and medians to ease into the fall. Condos and townhouses barely register at four sales, all at $1,500,000, which is a development-specific number, not a market tier you can shop.
